raw_landmarks.explanation: VIEW 3 is selected because it clearly shows the full profile of the axe head with its curved blade, the wooden haft, and the leather-wrapped butt. handle_butt is placed at the very end of the haft, visible as the dark, textured, rounded termination point. grip_center is located on the lower leather-wrapped section of the haft, where a palm would naturally rest, clearly visible and distinct from the blade. working_head is centered on the metal mass of the axe head, away from the edge. functional_edge is placed on the outer, curved, pale-colored cutting edge of the blade, clearly distinct from the working_head and visibly sharp in the render. All four landmarks are physically distinct and clearly visible within VIEW 3.

grips.evidence: The leather-wrapped lower haft is clearly visible in VIEW 3. The texture and wrapping are distinct from the bare wood above and the metal head. The point [0.31, 0.79] lies squarely on this wrapped section, which is the intended lower handhold.

The bare wooden shaft above the head is visible in VIEW 3. The point [0.48, 0.41] is located on this smooth, unwrapped section of the haft, clearly distinct from the blade and the lower grip, matching the upper handhold position.

features.evidence: The metal axe head is fully visible in VIEW 3. The origin [0.67, 0.3] is placed on the body of the head, and the direction_tip [0.73, 0.28] points outward along the visible curved, pale cutting edge. This direction clearly indicates the functional cutting surface, not the flat back or the handle.
